name: NCP361SNT1G
title: NCP361 / NCV361: USB positive overvoltage protection controller with internal PMOS FET and overcurrent protection
summary: A single-channel input protector for a USB VBUS line: a P-channel MOSFET between IN and OUT that is closed only while the input sits between an undervoltage lockout of 3.0 V and an overvoltage lockout of 5.675 V (typical), and that withstands up to 20 V on the input. The switch also opens on overcurrent (750 mA typical), turning on again after the ton delay of about 4 ms while the fault lasts, and on overtemperature. An active-low open-drain FLAG output reports faults and an active-low EN input turns the output off. It comes in a 2 x 2 mm UDFN6 and a TSOP-5; the NCV361 is the automotive version.
key_figures: 150 mV typ, 200 mV max at 500 mA
20 µA typ at 5.25 V, no load

notes: The NCV prefix marks the version for automotive and other uses that need unique site and change-control requirements; it is AEC-Q100 qualified and PPAP capable.
All three devices share the same thresholds: 750 mA overcurrent, 3.00 V UVLO and 5.675 V OVLO (typical).

pins.name: EN
pins.function: Enable, active low. A high level puts the part in shutdown with OUT cut off from IN; for normal operation hold it at GND or drive it from an I/O. Fault detection keeps running whatever its level.

pins.name: IN
pins.function: Input, tied to VBUS. Needs a low-ESR ceramic capacitor of 1 µF or more to GND.

pins.name: OUT
pins.function: Switched output, cut off from VBUS while the input is above the OVLO or below the UVLO threshold. Needs a 1 µF capacitor; both OUT pins are wired together on the board.

pins.name: FLAG
pins.function: Fault output, active low; pulled low when the input exceeds the OVLO threshold. Open drain, so a resistor to VCC must pull it up.

pins.name: PAD1
pins.function: Exposed pad, joined to the package tie bars. It may be tied to the ground plane to carry heat away and is never tied to any other potential.

circuits.title: Typical application circuit (UDFN pinout)
circuits.description: The NCP361 sits between a VBUS input and the protected rail. A 1 µF 25 V X5R 0603 ceramic (C1) decouples IN and a second one (C2) sits on the joined OUT pins. EN is wired straight to GND, so the switch is on whenever the input is inside the UVLO-OVLO window. The open-drain FLAG pin leaves as the FLAG signal and is pulled up through R1, 1 MΩ, from a separate FLAG supply by way of the two-pin part J2 (FLAG_State).

equations.name: DC current allowed by the thermal limit

where.RθJA: junction-to-ambient thermal resistance of the mounted package
where.RDSON: on-resistance of the internal PMOS FET

equations.note: With 260 °C/W (200 mm² of copper) and TA = 85 °C the result is 625 mA.

operation.text: An internal PMOS FET joins IN to OUT. While VBUS stays inside the window between UVLO and OVLO the output tracks the input, less the drop across the FET's RDS(on); outside the window the FET is off and the load is cut off. The input withstands positive overvoltage up to 20 V. No external switch is used.
A detection block watches input voltage, load current and die temperature and drives the switch. With VIN above OVLO or below UVLO the switch is open; with UVLO < VIN < OVLO it is closed.
On a rising input the output stays off until VIN passes 3.0 V nominal. FLAG is held low until the input reaches the UVLO threshold. The threshold has 70 mV of hysteresis against noise and transients.

Once VIN passes UVLO, the output ramps up and reaches 0.8 × Vin after ton (4.0 ms typical, 15 ms maximum), then settles at Vin - RDS(on) × I. FLAG rises past 1.2 V a time tstart after VIN crosses UVLO.

When VIN rises above OVLO the output turns off (toff, 0.7 µs typical, to Vout ≤ 0.3 V) and FLAG goes low (tstop, 1.0 µs typical, to FLAG ≤ 0.4 V). Both stay that way until VIN drops below OVLO less its 100 mV hysteresis. Between UVLO and OVLO the output follows the input; outside, it is at 0 V.

The current limit is set inside the part at 750 mA. Versions from 150 mA to 750 mA are possible by a metal option, available through onsemi. When the load current passes Ilim the FET turns off within 5 µs and FLAG goes low. The part then turns on again after the ton delay (4 ms typical) and keeps cycling on and off while the fault lasts, which limits dissipation; a system controller can count the FLAG events and turn the FET off with EN. Once the overload is removed, normal operation resumes on the next turn-on.

FLAG is pulled low when 1.2 V < Vin < UVLO, when Vin > OVLO, when the load current exceeds the limit, or when TJ > 150 °C, and is released in normal operation. It is an open-drain output and needs a pull-up resistor to VCC, typically 1 MΩ and at least 10 kΩ.

EN low or grounded allows normal operation; EN high cuts OUT off from IN, with Vout falling below 0.3 V within tdis (3.0 µs typical) of EN passing 1.2 V, while FLAG stays high. EN does not override an OVLO or UVLO fault: with EN high, FLAG still goes low when Vin leaves the window and returns high tstart after Vin is back inside it.
The FET turns off at a junction temperature of 150 °C (typical) and turns back on after the die cools by the 30 °C hysteresis; FLAG is low while the output is off.
With 1 µF mounted at the input on the board, the input meets IEC 61000-4-2 level 4: ±15 kV air discharge and ±8 kV contact discharge. HBM class 2, MM class B.

The internal PMOS FET is rated 500 mA. On the UDFN, PAD1 may be joined to the ground plane to improve heat transfer and must not be joined to any other potential. More copper area lowers RθJA and raises the current the part can carry: without added copper (305 °C/W) the DC current is 500 mA; with 200 mm² (260 °C/W) at 85 °C ambient it is 625 mA. The final thermal resistance is to be confirmed by measurement on the application board.
